title: Preselection-Encoded Weak-Value Interferometry for Optical-Rotation Metrology
authors: Jinyi Li, Juncheng Zheng, Yuntao Shen, Jiashu Liang, Sicheng Pan, Dongmei Li, Hengyan Wang, Wenqiang Zheng
abstract: Optical-rotation measurements benefit from increasing probe photon number, but their performance is often limited by detector saturation and technical noise in the optical readout. Here we introduce preselection-encoded weak-value amplification (PeWVA), in which the quantity of interest is encoded into the probe polarization before a downstream weak-value interferometer. This architecture separates the sensing interaction from the postselected readout, enabling tunable local amplification while reducing the optical power delivered to the detector. We show that PeWVA does not create additional Fisher information, but offers a practical advantage when detector dynamic range is limiting. We further analyze coherent stray light and phase fluctuations and show reduced conversion of these perturbations into equivalent rotation errors. Using an $^{87}$Rb $M_x$ atomic magnetometer, we experimentally demonstrate substantially improved magnetic-field readout under detector-constrained conditions using both transimpedance-amplified and avalanche photodiodes. The experiments also confirm reduced susceptibility to vapor-cell-induced stray light and interferometer phase modulation. These results establish PeWVA as a detector-constrained optical readout strategy with enhanced tolerance to representative interferometric perturbations.
summary: This paper introduces Preselection-Encoded Weak-Value Amplification (PeWVA) as a novel readout strategy for optical-rotation metrology. By encoding the measurement parameter into the probe polarization before a weak-value interferometer, PeWVA mitigates detector saturation issues common in high-precision sensing. Experimental validation using an atomic magnetometer confirms that PeWVA significantly improves magnetic-field readout performance under realistic, detector-constrained conditions.
main_problem: Optical-rotation measurements are limited by detector saturation and technical noise when increasing probe photon number, despite the benefit of high photon numbers for precision.
main_result: The proposed Preselection-Encoded Weak-Value Amplification (PeWVA) technique provides a practical advantage by allowing high-flux sensing while keeping detected power within detector limits, leading to substantially improved magnetic-field readout.
method: The authors introduce PeWVA, which encodes the measured quantity into the probe polarization *before* a weak-value interferometer, separating sensing from readout.
model_or_system: The experiment uses an ${}^{87}	ext{Rb } M_x$ atomic magnetometer platform, employing polarization interferometry and weak-value measurement principles.
key_observables: Magnetic-field noise floor ($	ext{pT}/\sqrt{	ext{Hz}}$), visibility ($V$), and Fisher Information ($F(	heta)$).
important_parameters: Detector saturation limit, weak-coupling parameter ($D$), and incident photon number ($N_{ph}$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the ability to separate the sensing interaction from the postselected readout, and that the primary limitation is detector dynamic range rather than fundamental quantum limits.

paper_structure: The paper first introduces the problem of detector limitations in optical metrology. It then develops the PeWVA theory, comparing it mathematically to standard interferometry (SI) using Fisher Information. Finally, it presents experimental results using an atomic magnetometer, demonstrating noise reduction and improved robustness against stray light.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses practical limitations in quantum sensing by modifying the measurement readout scheme. The concept of separating sensing and readout via preselection is highly relevant for designing robust quantum optical sensors.

figures.caption: Figure 1. Schematic of the PeWVA polarization- interferometric readout. The sensing stage prepares the parameter-dependent state |χ(θ)⟩before the interferometer. The opposite polarization rotations ±D provide the fixed weak coupling, ς denotes the relative phase between the two interferometer arms, and the final polarizer performs the postselection onto |P⟩. Removing the final polarizer gives the standard-interferometric (SI) reference. PBS, polarizing beam splitter; BS, beam splitter.

Figure 2. Calculated visibility for SI and PeWVA as a func- tion of the polarization angle θ. For SI, D = 22.5◦maximizes the local response. For PeWVA, decreasing D enhances the local response near the operating point while narrowing the usable range, illustrating the trade-off between local amplifi- cation and dynamic range.
Figure 3. Fisher information as a function of D and θ for (a) SI and (b) PeWVA. At fixed incident photon number, both schemes attain the same ideal maximum FI of 4N.

Figure 4. Calculated equivalent OR errors for SI and PeWVA under representative interferometric perturbations. (a) and (b) Equivalent rotation error ∆θs induced by coherent stray light as a function of the relative stray-field amplitude r and phase δ for SI and PeWVA, respectively. (c) and (d) Equiv- alent OR error induced by relative interferometer-phase fluc- tuations for SI and PeWVA, respectively. The parameters are θ = 45◦and D = 22.5◦for SI, and θ = 0.64◦and D = 0.3◦

Figure 5. Experimental configuration of the 87Rb Mx atomic magnetometer and downstream PeWVA readout. The vapor cell is located inside a five-layer magnetic shield and is ad- dressed by orthogonal pump and probe beams. The static field B0 is applied along the pump direction and the rf field Brf along the probe direction. After the cell, the probe enters the polarization interferometer, where HWP1 and HWP2 in- troduce opposite weak rotations ±D, the phase controller sets the relative arm phase, and the final polarizer performs the postselection. Removing the postselection polarizer realizes the SI reference. HWP, half-wave plate; P, polarizer; PBS, polarizing beam splitter; M, mirror; PC,...
